## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:records` · `pm:queue`. Direction: `action:menu` consumes the host's `disabled` by name, the objectui#9131 rule. Serial after objectui#11168 slice 1

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-30T08:53Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-menu.tsx` ⇒ `domain:ui`, the lane that fixed objectui#9131.

**Re-read on objectui `origin/main` `e978ed5eaf`.**
- `action-menu.tsx` renders `disabled={loading}` at `:369`, then `{...rest}` at `:371`.
- `action-button.tsx` consumes `hostDisabled` by name (`:103`, `:374`).

**Why p2.** It takes objectui#9131's grade: the same shape, on the third action renderer. A pressable trigger during an in-flight action lets a second execution start (a duplicate record, a duplicate send), on every schema-rendered page that uses `action:menu`. It was measured once, in a probe.

**Direction.** As the card states, confirmed:
- `action:menu` takes the host's forwarded `disabled` by name: `disabled={hostDisabled || loading || <its own gate>}`. `{...rest}` can then no longer carry `disabled`.
- **One rule across `action:button`, `action:icon` and `action:menu`.** ⛔ No second convention.
- **`action:group`** (`action-group.tsx:226`, `:390`) is measured in the same pass. If the forwarded `disabled` reaches its wrapper, it is fixed here the same way. If not, the reading goes in the report.
- **Pins,** through the real `SchemaRenderer`:
  - an in-flight member keeps the trigger disabled, and it re-enables when the action settles;
  - a host-disabled menu stays disabled;
  - a direct registry mount agrees (the control).

**Serial.** `action-menu.tsx` and `action-group.tsx` are in objectui#11168 slice 1's in-flight surface (`domain:spec`, `huangyiirene`). This card is dispatched after that slice merges, or rides it if that seat agrees in writing on objectui#11168.

`finding` comes off at grading.

The dev stops on a breach and explains it in the report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (default judgment tier; `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` answers no path-derived mandate for these paths)
Clause-②: no
Thread-read: 5907713921
Serial constraints cleared: objectui#11168 slice 1 (PR objectui#11185), the serial predecessor triage named, merged as `3cc4fe567b` 2026-09-30T12:52:36Z; `action-menu.tsx:369` / `:371` are unchanged by it (read at objectui `origin/main` `cfc9b6db98`). No open PR touches `packages/components/src/renderers/action/**` (read 2026-09-30T13:33Z over the open objectui PRs). objectui#11212 (this seat, Rider 1 residue of objectui#4421) shares `action-group.tsx`; fold-or-serial answers **serial, this card first**: the defects differ (a forwarded `disabled` overwriting the loading state vs. the fault policy of permission predicates while the payload loads), so fold gate ① fails, and this card is older at the same grade. objectui#11212 re-points its `Blocked-by:` to this card.

Scope: triage's direction `5907713921` verbatim, "`action:menu` takes the host's forwarded `disabled` by name: `disabled={hostDisabled || loading || <its own gate>}`", "**One rule across `action:button`, `action:icon` and `action:menu`.** ⛔ No second convention.", and `action:group` measured in the same pass.
`Clause-②: no` — why: a runtime fix inside one renderer; no schema accept or reject changes and no public export or type member is added or removed.

The spec's `ActionMenuPropsSchema` declares no own gate, so that is the complete OR |

**Deviations, accepted as the record answers them:** the full `packages/components` run is on `b9967bba99`, and the two later commits touch only the test file and the changeset (verified); the other three are process and naming.

**Out-of-scope findings:**
- `action:menu` spreads the raw `rest` onto its trigger (and inline `action:group` onto its wrapper), where `action:button` / `action:icon` filter through `toFormControlDomProps` → **Acceptance notes** (read from source, not measured; `disabled` is now consumed by name on all four, so nothing forwarded by the host reaches the DOM through it).
- `autoTrigger` members of a menu disabled from mount still run, since `useAutoTriggerOnce` takes only the visibility verdict, as on `action:button` → **Acceptance notes** (seen once, not reproduced as a user-facing defect; whether an enablement verdict should also stop an auto-trigger is a product question no card asks today).
